title: First-Order Topological FFLO Transition and Superconducting Diode Sign Reversal in Altermagnetic Nanowires
authors: Bo Fu, Kaizhi Bai, Chang-An Li, Shun-Qing Shen
abstract: Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) state conventionally emerges via a second-order phase transition driven by finite magnetization. Here we show that a spin-orbit-coupled nanowire proximitized to $d$-wave altermagnets -- with zero net magnetization -- can realize topological FFLO states through a first-order transition, marked by a sharp sign-reversing superconducting diode effect. The altermagnetic field generates band-resolved competing pairing channels, giving rise to a double-valley free energy landscape whose global minimum switches discontinuously. It consequently leads to a first-order topological FFLO transition with simultaneous jumps in the Cooper pairing amplitude and finite center-of-mass momentum. Remarkably, this discontinuous topological reconfiguration substantially enhances the diode efficiency and drives a characteristic sharp sign reversal across the transition. The mechanism of such exotic phenomena is captured by Ginzburg--Landau theory. Our results provide a field-free altermagnetic route to topological FFLO states and identify their direct transport fingerprint.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates that proximity coupling to altermagnets can induce a first-order transition into a topological FFLO state in nanowires. This abrupt phase change is predicted to manifest as a sharp sign reversal in the superconducting diode effect, offering a novel transport fingerprint for these exotic quantum states.
main_problem: The research investigates realizing a first-order topological Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) transition in superconducting nanowires proximitized to altermagnets.
main_result: This first-order transition is shown to be marked by discontinuous jumps in the pairing amplitude and momentum, which simultaneously drives a sharp sign reversal in the superconducting diode efficiency ($\eta$).
method: The analysis employs Ginzburg-Landau theory applied to the free energy functional derived from mean-field calculations of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is a spin-orbit-coupled nanowire coupled to a $d$-wave altermagnetic substrate. The physics is modeled using BdG Hamiltonians and analyzed via minimizing an effective free energy functional $\Omega(\mathbf{q}, \Delta)$.
key_observables: Topological invariant ($Z_2$), superconducting diode efficiency ($\eta$), optimal pairing amplitude ($\Delta_{opt}$), and pairing momentum ($\mathbf{q}_{opt}$).
important_parameters: Altermagnetic coupling strength ($J_A$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field approximations, the use of a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau functional, and sometimes quadratic approximations for simplicity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the band structure evolution, the calculation of the topological invariant across phases (cFFLO $	o$ tFFLO), and crucially, show how the superconducting diode efficiency ($\eta$) exhibits a sharp sign reversal at the first-order transition boundary.
paper_structure: The paper develops the Hamiltonian for the system, derives the necessary free energy functional via mean-field theory, maps out the phase diagram showing three FFLO states (cFFLO, nFFLO, tFFLO), and finally uses GL analysis to link the first-order nature of the transition to the observable sign reversal in $\eta$.
why_interesting: The connection between topological quantum phases (characterized by $Z_2$ invariants) and measurable transport properties like diode efficiency provides a concrete, experimentally accessible signature for exotic superconducting states.
